draft.title: The rock cycle
card: The rock cycle is the set of processes that turn rock of one type into another. Some steps happen in seconds, such as lava cooling in an eruption. Others, such as burial and metamorphism, take millions of years.
Surface processes
Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Erosion moves the pieces away, and deposition drops them in a new place. Layers of sediment that are buried and cemented become sedimentary rock.
Underground processes
Heat and pressure change buried rock into metamorphic rock without melting it. If the rock gets hot enough to melt, it becomes magma. When magma cools, it forms igneous rock.
Uplift
Uplift pushes rock from deep underground up towards the surface. There it can be weathered, and the cycle goes on.
draft.remember: There is no single path: any rock can change into any type, in seconds during an eruption or over millions of years.

a.q: A strong wind lifts loose sand grains off a weathered cliff and carries them far inland. Which rock cycle process is moving the grains?
a.why: Erosion is the process that moves weathered pieces of rock, for example by wind or a river. Deposition is tempting, but it is when the pieces are dropped, not when they are carried. Weathering breaks the rock up before it is moved.
a.clue: Are the grains being broken up, moved or dropped?

b.q: Waves pound a cliff of igneous rock beside the sea. Which order of processes could turn this rock into sedimentary rock?
opts: Heating, melting, cooling, then slow uplift
Heat, pressure, burial, then slow uplift
b.why: The rock is first broken into pieces, then moved, then dropped in layers that are buried and cemented. The reversed order is tempting, but pieces cannot be moved or dropped before weathering makes them. Melting and cooling would give igneous rock, and heat and pressure would give metamorphic rock.
b.clue: What has to happen to solid rock before any pieces can be moved?
